title: Finite-colimit preservation in the top nonzero right derived degree
statement: Let C,D be abelian categories, C have enough injectives, and F:C→D be additive and left exact. If R^(n+1)F(M)=0 for every object M, then R^n F preserves finite colimits.

source.place: Section 1, long exact cohomology sequence; coefficient argument of blueprint sk-prop-a1-kummer.

proof.text: For each short exact sequence, use exists_rightDerived_full_long_exact. It gives exactness at the middle degree-n term. The connecting map out of its last degree-n term has zero target by the hypothesis, so exactness there makes the preceding map an epimorphism. Apply the standard Mathlib criterion preservesFiniteColimits_iff_forall_exact_map_and_epi for additive functors between abelian categories.

theorem rightDerived_preservesFiniteColimits_of_succ_isZero
    {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₂} D]
    [Abelian C] [EnoughInjectives C] [Abelian D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (n : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ M : C, IsZero ((F.rightDerived (n + 1)).obj M)) :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (F.rightDerived n)
